paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 26 to 35 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 26 至 35 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Did Sarah Josepha Hale write “Mary 's Little Lamb,” the eternal nursery rhyme (儿歌) about a girl named Mary with a stubborn lamb? This is still dispute , but it’s clear that the woman 26 for writing it was one of America 's most fascinating 27 _. In honor of the poem 's publication on May 24，1830，here’s more about the
28 author 's life.

Hale wasn’t just a writer, she was also a 29 social advocate, and she was particularly 30_ with an ideal New England, which she associated with abundant Thanksgiving meals that she claimed had “a deep moral influence.” she began a nationwide 31 to have a national holiday declared that would bring families together while

celebrating the 32 festivals. In 1863, after 17 years of advocacy including letters to five presidents，Hale got it. President Abraham Lincoln, during the Civil War, issued a 33 setting aside the last Thursday in November for the holiday.

The true authorship of “Mary’s Little Lamb” is disputed.. According to New England Historical Society, Hale wrote only one part of the poem, but claimed authorship. Regardless of the author, it seems that the poem was

34 by a real event. When young Mary Sawyer was followed to school by a lamb in 1816, it caused some problems. A bystander named John Roulstone wrote a poem about the event, then, at some point, Hale herself seems to have helped write it. However, if a 1916 piece by her great-niece is to be trusted, Hale claimed for the 35 of her life that “Some other people pretended that someone else wrote the poem”.

Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Grow Plants Without Water
paragraphs.translationZh: 不用水种植植物

paragraphs.sourceText: A) . Ever since humanity began to farm our own food, we've faced the unpredictable rain that is both friend and enemy. It comes and goes without much warning, and a field of lush (茂盛的) leafy greens one year can dry up and blow away the next. Food security and fortunes depend on sufficient rain, and nowhere more so than in Africa, where 96% of farmland depends on rain instead of the irrigation common in more developed places. It has consequences : South Africa's ongoing drought— the worst in three decades— will cost at least a quarter of its com crop this year.
paragraphs.translationZh: A).自从人类开始自己种植食物以来，我们就面临着不可预测的雨水，它既是朋友也是敌人。它来来去去都没有太多预兆，一年里郁郁葱葱的绿叶蔬菜可能会在下一年干涸并被风吹走。粮食安全和财富取决于充足的降雨，在非洲尤其如此，那里 96% 的农田依赖雨水，而不是较发达地区常见的灌溉。它产生了后果：南非持续的干旱——三十年来最严重的干旱——将导致今年至少四分之一的玉米作物损失。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) . Biologist Jill Farrant of the University of Cape Town in South Africa says that nature has plenty of answers for people who want to grow crops in places with unpredictable rainfall. She is hard at work finding a way to take traits from rare wild plants that adapt to extreme dry weather and use them in food crops. As the earth's climate changes and rainfall becomes even less predictable in some places, those answers will grow even more valuable."The type of farming I'm aiming for is literally so that people can survive as it's going to get more and more dry,"Farrant says.
paragraphs.translationZh: B).南非开普敦大学的生物学家吉尔·法兰特表示，对于那些想要在降雨量不可预测的地方种植农作物的人们来说，大自然有很多答案。她正在努力寻找一种方法，从适应极端干燥天气的稀有野生植物中获取性状，并将其用于粮食作物。随着地球气候变化和某些地方的降雨量变得更加难以预测，这些答案将变得更加有价值。“我所追求的农业类型实际上是为了让人们能够在天气变得越来越干燥的情况下生存，”法兰特说。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) . Extreme conditions produce extremely tough plants. In the rusty red deserts of South Africa, steep-sided rocky hills called inselbergs rear up from the plains like the bones of the earth. The hills are remnants of an earlier geological era, scraped bare of most soil and exposed to the elements. Yet on these and similar formations in deserts around the world, a few fierce plants have adapted to endure under ever-changing conditions.
paragraphs.translationZh: C).极端的条件会产生极其坚韧的植物。在南非的锈红色沙漠中，被称为岛山的陡峭岩石山丘像地球的骨头一样从平原上拔地而起。这些山丘是早期地质时代的遗迹，大部分土壤被刮掉，暴露在自然环境中。然而，在世界各地沙漠中的这些和类似地层上，一些凶猛的植物已经适应了不断变化的条件。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) . Farrant calls them resurrection plants (复苏植物) . During months without water under a harsh sun. They wither, shrink and contract until they look like a pile of dead gray leaves. But rainfall can revive them in a matter of hours. Her time-lapse (间歇性拍摄的) videos of the revivals look like someone playing a tape of the plant's death in reverse.
paragraphs.translationZh: D）。法兰特称它们为复活植物（respiratory plant）。在严酷的阳光下几个月没有水。它们枯萎、萎缩、收缩，直到看起来像一堆枯死的灰色树叶。但降雨可以在几个小时内使它们恢复活力。她拍摄的复苏延时视频看起来就像有人倒放植物死亡的磁带。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) . The big difference between "drought-tolerant" plants and these tough plants: metabolism. Many different kinds of plants have developed tactics to weather dry spells. Some plants store reserves of water to see them through a drought ; others send roots deep down to subsurface water supplies. But once these plants use up their stored reserve or tap out the underground supply, they cease growing and start to die. They may be able to handle a drought of some length, and many people use the term "drought tolerant" to describe such plants, but they never actually stop needing to consume water, so Farrant prefers to call them drought resistant.
paragraphs.translationZh: E）。 “耐旱”植物和这些坚韧植物的最大区别在于：新陈代谢。许多不同种类的植物已经发展出应对干旱的策略。有些植物会储存水分以度过干旱；有些植物会储存水分以应对干旱。其他的则将根深深扎入地下水源。但一旦这些植物用完储存的储备或耗尽地下供应，它们就会停止生长并开始死亡。它们可能能够应对一定时间的干旱，许多人使用“耐旱”一词来描述此类植物，但它们实际上从未停止需要消耗水，因此法兰特更喜欢称它们为抗旱植物。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) . Resurrection plants, defined as those capable of recovering from holding less than 0.1 grams of water per gram of dry mass, are different. They lack water-storing structures, and their existence on rock faces prevents them from tapping groundwater, so they have instead developed the ability to change their metabolism .When they detect an extended dry period, they divert their metabolisms, producing sugars and certain stress-associated proteins and other materials in their tissues. As the plant dries, these resources take on first the properties of honey, then rubber, and finally enter a glass-like state that is "the most stable state that the plant can maintain," Farrant says. That slows the plant's metabolism and protects its dried-out tissues. The plants also change shape, shrinking to minimize the surface area through which their remaining water might evaporate. They can recover from months and years without water, depending on the species.
paragraphs.translationZh: F).复活植物的定义是那些能够从每克干物质中含有少于 0.1 克水的植物中恢复过来，这是不同的。它们缺乏储水结构，而且它们存在于岩石表面，无法利用地下水，因此它们反而发展出了改变新陈代谢的能力。当它们检测到干旱期延长时，它们会改变新陈代谢，在组织中产生糖和某些与压力相关的蛋白质和其他物质。当植物干燥时，这些资源首先呈现蜂蜜的特性，然后是橡胶，最后进入玻璃状状态，这是“植物可以维持的最稳定的状态”，法兰特说。这会减慢植物的新陈代谢并保护其干燥的组织。植物也会改变形状，收缩以尽量减少剩余水分可能蒸发的表面积。根据物种的不同，它们可以在数月甚至数年没有水的情况下恢复。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) . What else can do this dry-out-and-revive trick? Seeds-almost all of them. At the start of her career, Farrant studied . recalcitrant seeds (执拗性种子) ," such as avocados, coffee and lychee. While tasty, such seeds are delicate--they cannot bud and grow if they dry out (as you may know if you've ever tried to grow a tree from an avocado pit). In the seed world, that makes them rare, because most seeds from flowering plants are quite robust. Most seeds can wait out the dry, unwelcoming seasons until conditions are right and they sprout (发芽). Yet once they start growing, such plants seem not to retain the ability to hit the pause button on metabolism in their stems or leaves.
paragraphs.translationZh: G）。还有什么可以实现这种干燥和恢复的技巧呢？种子——几乎全部。在她的职业生涯开始时，法兰特学习了。执拗性种子，如牛油果、咖啡和荔枝。虽然美味，但这些种子很脆弱——如果干燥，它们就无法发芽和生长（如果你曾经尝试过从牛油果坑里种一棵树，你可能知道这一点）。在种子世界中，这使得它们很稀有，因为大多数开花植物的种子都非常坚固。大多数种子可以等待干燥、不受欢迎的季节，直到条件合适并发芽。然而，一旦它们开始生长，这些植物似乎就不再保留茎或叶新陈代谢暂停按钮的能力。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) . After completing her Ph. D. on seeds, Farrant began investigating whether it might be possible to isolate the properties that make most seeds so resilient (迅速恢复活力的) and transfer them to other plant tissues. What Farrant and others have found over the past two decades is that there are many genes involved in resurrection plants' response to dryness. Many of them are the same that regulate how seeds become dryness-tolerant while still attached to their parent plants. Now they are trying to figure out what molecular signaling processes activate those seed-building genes in resurrection plants— and how to reproduce them in crops."Most genes are regulated by a master set of genes,"Farrant says."We're looking at gene promoters and what would be their master switch."
paragraphs.translationZh: H）。在获得种子博士学位后，法兰特开始研究是否有可能分离出大多数种子具有快速恢复活力的特性，并将其转移到其他植物组织中。法兰特和其他人在过去二十年中发现，有许多基因参与复活植物对干旱的反应。其中许多是相同的，它们调节种子如何变得耐旱，同时仍然附着在其母体植物上。现在，他们正试图找出哪些分子信号传导过程激活了复活植物中的种子构建基因，以及如何在作物中繁殖它们。“大多数基因都受到一组主基因的调节，”法兰特说。“我们正在研究基因启动子以及它们的主开关。”

paragraphs.sourceText: I) . Once Farrant and her colleagues feel they have a better sense of which switches to throw, they will have to find the best way to do so in useful crops."I'm trying three methods of breeding,"Farrant says : conventional, genetic modification arid gene editing. She says she is aware that plenty of people do not want to eat genetically modified crops, but she is pushing ahead with every available tool until one works. Farmers and consumers alike can choose whether or not to use whichever version prevails :"I'm giving people an option. "
paragraphs.translationZh: 我）。一旦法兰特和她的同事们觉得他们对要扔掉哪些开关有了更好的认识，他们就必须找到在有用作物中实现这一点的最佳方法。“我正在尝试三种育种方法，”法兰特说：传统的、基因改造和基因编辑。她说她知道很多人不想吃转基因作物，但她正在推动一切可用的工具，直到其中一种有效。农民和消费者都可以选择是否使用流行的版本：“我给人们一个选择。 ”

paragraphs.sourceText: J) . Farrant and others in the resurrection business got together last year to discuss the best species of resurrection plant to use as a lab model. Just like medical researchers use rats to test ideas for human medical treatments, botanists use plants that are relatively easy to grow in a lab or greenhouse setting to test their ideas for related species. The Queensland rock violet is one of the best studied resurrection plants so far, with a draft genome (基因图谱) published last year by a Chinese team. Also last year, Farrant and colleagues published a detailed molecular study of another candidate, Xerophyta viscosa, a tough-as-nail south African plant with lily-like flowers, and she says that a genome is on the way. one or both of these models will help researchers test their ideas — so far mostly done in the lab— on test plots.
paragraphs.translationZh: J）。法兰特和复活行业的其他人去年聚在一起讨论用作实验室模型的最佳复活植物种类。就像医学研究人员使用老鼠来测试人类医学治疗的想法一样，植物学家使用相对容易在实验室或温室环境中生长的植物来测试他们对相关物种的想法。昆士兰岩紫罗兰是迄今为止研究最深入的复活植物之一，中国团队去年发布了基因组草案（基因图谱）。同样在去年，Farrant 和同事发表了对另一种候选植物 Xerophyta viscosa 的详细分子研究，这是一种坚硬如指甲的南非植物，开着百合状的花朵，她说基因组正在研究中。这些模型中的一个或两个将帮助研究人员在测试地块上测试他们的想法（到目前为止大部分是在实验室中完成的）。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) . Understanding the basic science first is key. There are good reasons why crop plants do not use dryness defenses already. For instance, there's a high energy cost in switching from a regular metabolism to an almost-no-water metabolism. It will also be necessary to understand what sort of yield farmers might expect and to establish the plant's safety."The yield is never going to be high,"Farrant says, so these plants will be targeted not at Iowa farmers trying to squeeze more cash
paragraphs.translationZh: K）。首先了解基础科学是关键。农作物不使用干燥防御措施是有充分理由的。例如，从常规新陈代谢转变为几乎无水新陈代谢的能量成本很高。还必须了解农民可能期望什么样的产量并确定工厂的安全性。法兰特说，“产量永远不会很高，”因此这些工厂的目标不是试图榨取更多现金的爱荷华州农民。

paragraphs.sourceText: out of high-yield fields, but subsistence farmers who need help to survive a drought like the present one in South Africa."My vision is for the subsistence farmer," Farrant says."I'm targeting crops that are of African value. ".
paragraphs.translationZh: 法兰特说：“我的愿景是为自给自足的农民服务。”“我的目标是对非洲有价值的作物。”

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. There are a couple of plants tough and adaptable enough to survive on bare rocky hills and in deserts.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 有几种植物坚韧且适应性强，足以在光秃秃的岩石山丘和沙漠中生存。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Farrant is trying to isolate genes in resurrection plants and reproduce them in crops.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. Farrant 正在尝试分离复活植物中的基因并将其复制到农作物中。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Farmers in South Africa are more at the mercy of nature, especially inconsistent rainfall.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 南非的农民更多地受到自然的摆布，尤其是降雨量的不稳定。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Resurrection crops are most likely to be the choice of subsistence farmers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 复活作物最有可能成为自给农民的选择。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40.Even though many plants have developed various tactics to cope with dry weather, they cannot survive a prolonged drought.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40.尽管许多植物已经发展出各种应对干燥天气的策略，但它们无法在长期干旱中生存。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Despite consumer resistance, researchers are pushing ahead with genetic modification of crops.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 尽管消费者抵制，研究人员仍在推进作物基因改造。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Most seeds can pull through dry spells and begin growing when conditions are ripe, but once this process starts, it cannot be held back.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 大多数种子都能渡过干旱期，并在条件成熟时开始生长，但一旦这个过程开始，就无法阻止。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Farrant is working hard to cultivate food crops that call survive extreme dryness by studying the traits of rare wild plants.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 法兰特正在通过研究稀有野生植物的性状，努力培育能够在极端干旱条件下生存的粮食作物。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. By adjusting their metabolism, resurrection plants can recover from an extended period of drought.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 通过调整新陈代谢，复活植物可以从长期干旱中恢复过来。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Resurrection plants can come back to life in a short time after a rainfall.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 复活植物可以在降雨后短时间内恢复生机。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Human memory is notoriously unreliable. Even people with the sharpest facial-recognition skills can only remember so much.
paragraphs.translationZh: 众所周知，人类的记忆是不可靠的。即使具有最敏锐的面部识别能力的人也只能记住这么多。

paragraphs.sourceText: It's tough to quantify how good a person is at remembering. No one really knows how many different faces someone can recall, for example, but various estimates tend to hover in the thousands-based on the number of acquaintances a person might have.
paragraphs.translationZh: 很难量化一个人的记忆力有多强。例如，没有人真正知道一个人能回忆起多少张不同的面孔，但根据一个人可能拥有的熟人数量，各种估计往往徘徊在数千张上。

paragraphs.sourceText: Machines aren't limited this way, Give the right computer a massive database of faces, and it can process what it sees-then recognize a face it's told to find-with remarkable speed and precision. This skill is what supports the enormous promise of facial-recognition software in the 2lst century. It's also what makes contemporary surveillance systems so scary.
paragraphs.translationZh: 机器不受这种方式的限制，给正确的计算机一个庞大的人脸数据库，它就可以以惊人的速度和精度处理它所看到的内容，然后识别它被告知要找到的人脸。这项技能支撑着面部识别软件在 2 世纪的巨大前景。这也是当代监控系统如此可怕的原因。

paragraphs.sourceText: The thing is, machines still have limitations when it comes to facial recognition. And scientists are only just beginning to understand what those constraints are. To begin to figure out how computers are struggling, researchers at the University of Washington created a massive database of faces- they call it MegaFace- and tested a variety of facial-recognition algorithms (算法) as they scaled up in complexity. The idea was to test the machines on a database that included up to 1 million different images of nearly 700,000 different people-and not just a large database featuring a relatively small number of different faces, more consistent with what's been used in other research.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题是，机器在面部识别方面仍然存在局限性。科学家们才刚刚开始了解这些限制是什么。为了弄清楚计算机是如何陷入困境的，华盛顿大学的研究人员创建了一个庞大的人脸数据库——他们称之为 MegaFace——并测试了各种面部识别算法（算法），因为它们的复杂性不断扩大。这个想法是在一个数据库上测试机器，该数据库包含近 700,000 个人的多达 100 万张不同图像，而不仅仅是一个包含相对少量不同面孔的大型数据库，与其他研究中使用的数据更加一致。

paragraphs.sourceText: As the databases grew, machine accuracy dipped across the board. Algorithms that were right 95% of the time when they were dealing with a 13, 000-image database, for example, were accurate about 70% of the time when confronted with 1 million images. That's still pretty good, says one of the researchers, Ira Kemelmacher-Shlizerman."Much better than we expected, "she said.
paragraphs.translationZh: 随着数据库的增长，机器的准确性全面下降。例如，在处理 13, 000 张图像的数据库时，算法的正确率达到 95%，而在处理 100 万张图像时，算法的正确率约为 70%。研究人员之一艾拉·凯梅尔马赫-什利泽曼 (Ira Kemelmacher-Shlizerman) 表示，这仍然相当不错。“比我们预期的要好得多，”她说。

paragraphs.sourceText: Machines also had difficulty adjusting for people who look a lot alike-either doppelgangers(长相极相似的人),whom the machine would have trouble identifying as two separate people, or the same person who appeared in different photos at different ages or in different lighting, whom the 第6 页 machine would incorrectly view as separate people.
paragraphs.translationZh: 机器也很难适应长相非常相似的人——要么是长相极相似的人，机器很难将他们识别为两个不同的人，要么是同一个人出现在不同年龄或不同光线下的不同照片中，机器会错误地将他们视为不同的人。

paragraphs.sourceText: "Once we scale up, algorithms must be sensitive to tiny changes in identities and at the same time invariant to lighting, pose, age, "Kemelmacher-Shlizerman said.
paragraphs.translationZh: “一旦我们扩大规模，算法必须对身份的微小变化敏感，同时对光照、姿势、年龄保持不变，”Kemelmacher-Shlizerman 说。

paragraphs.sourceText: The trouble is, for many of the researchers who'd like to design systems to address these challenges, massive datasets for experimentation just don't exist--at least, not in formats that are accessible to academic researchers.Training sets like the ones Google and Facebook have are private. There are no public databases that contain millions of faces. MegaFace's creators say it's the largest publicly available facial-recognition dataset out there.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题是，对于许多想要设计系统来应对这些挑战的研究人员来说，用于实验的大量数据集并不存在——至少不存在学术研究人员可以访问的格式。谷歌和 Facebook 等训练集是私有的。没有包含数百万张面孔的公共数据库。 MegaFace 的创建者表示，它是目前最大的公开面部识别数据集。

paragraphs.sourceText: “An ultimate face recognition algorithm should perform with billions of people in a dataset, ”the researchers wrote.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究人员写道：“最终的人脸识别算法应该适用于数据集中的数十亿人。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: There’re currently 21.5 million students in America, and many will be funding their college on borrowed money. Given that there's now over $1.3 trillion in student loans on the books, it's pretty clear that many students are far from sensible. The average student's debt upon graduation now approaches $40, 000, and as college becomes ever more expensive, calls to make it "free" are multiplying. Even Hillary Clinton says that when it comes to college, "Costs won't be a barrier."
paragraphs.translationZh: 目前美国有 2150 万学生，其中许多人将靠借钱资助他们的大学。鉴于目前账面上的学生贷款超过 1.3 万亿美元，很明显，许多学生远不明智。现在，学生毕业时的平均债务接近 40, 000 美元，而且随着大学费用变得越来越昂贵，要求大学“免费”的呼声越来越高。就连希拉里·克林顿也表示，谈到上大学，“费用不会成为障碍。”

paragraphs.sourceText: But the only way college could be free is if the faculty and staff donated their time, the buildings required no maintenance, and campuses required no utilities. As long as it's impossible to produce something from nothing costs are absolutely a barrier.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但大学免费的唯一途径是教职员工贡献自己的时间，建筑物不需要维护，校园不需要公用事业。只要不可能从无到有，成本就绝对是一个障碍。

paragraphs.sourceText: The actual question we debate is who should pay for people to go to college. If taxpayers are to bear the cost of forgiving student loans, shouldn't they have a say in how their money is used?
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们争论的实际问题是谁应该支付人们上大学的费用。如果纳税人要承担免除学生贷款的成本，他们难道不应该对如何使用自己的钱有发言权吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: At least taxpayers should be able to decide what students will study on the public dime. If we're going to force taxpayers to foot the bill for college degrees, students should only study those subjects that’re of greatest benefit to taxpayers. After all, students making their own choices in this respect is what caused the problem in the first place. We simply don't need more poetry, gender studies, or sociology majors. How do we know which subjects benefit society? Easy.
paragraphs.translationZh: 至少纳税人应该能够决定学生用公共资金学习什么。如果我们要强迫纳税人为大学学位买单，学生就应该只学习那些对纳税人最有利的科目。毕竟，学生自己在这方面的选择才是造成问题的根源。我们根本不需要更多的诗歌、性别研究或社会学专业。我们如何知道哪些科目有益于社会？简单的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Average starting salaries give a clear indication of what type of training society needs its new workers to have. Certainly, there're benefits to a college major beyond the job a student can perform. But if we're talking about the benefits to society, the only thing that matters is what the major enables the student to produce for society. And the value of what the student can produce is reflected in the wage employers are willing to pay the student to produce it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 平均起薪清楚地表明社会需要新工人接受什么类型的培训。当然，大学专业的好处超出了学生所能完成的工作。但如果我们谈论对社会的好处，唯一重要的是该专业能让学生为社会创造什么。学生产出的价值反映在雇主愿意支付给学生产出的工资上。

paragraphs.sourceText: A low wage for elementary school teachers, however, doesn't mean elementary education isn’t important. It simply means there're too many elementary school teachers already.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，小学教师的工资低并不意味着基础教育不重要。这仅仅意味着小学教师已经太多了。

paragraphs.sourceText: Meanwhile, there're few who're willing and able to perform jobs requiring a petroleum engineering major, so the value of one more of those people is very high
paragraphs.translationZh: 同时，愿意并且能够从事需要石油工程专业的工作的人很少，因此多一个这样的人的价值非常高

paragraphs.sourceText: So we can have taxpayers pick up students' tuition in exchange for dictating what those students will study. Or we can allow students both to choose their majors and pay for their education themselves. But in the end ,one of two things is true:
paragraphs.translationZh: 因此，我们可以让纳税人承担学生的学费，以换取决定这些学生将学习什么。或者我们可以允许学生自己选择专业并支付学费。但最终，有两件事是正确的：

paragraphs.sourceText: Either a college major is worth its cost or it isn't. If yes, taxpayer financing isn't needed If not taxpayer financing isn't desirable. Either way, taxpayers have no business paying for students' college education.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大学专业要么物有所值，要么不物有所值。如果是，则不需要纳税人融资；如果不是，则不需要纳税人融资。不管怎样，纳税人无权支付学生的大学教育费用。
